picks.file: PPN834537656 Altona von der Nord-Seite gesehen (1860).jpg
picks.what: Altona from the north, colored lithograph (Staatsbibliothek Hamburg)
picks.why: color general view over the town’s roofs, church towers and windmills, with a tree-lined street in front; mount and caption trimmed

gaps: P0–P3: nothing usable; P5: nothing usable; P6: nothing (modern hits are Blankenese)
notes: #8 (Heinrich Berger, 1850) is a strong black-and-white alternative for P4: Altona’s Elbe riverfront on the left with Hamburg’s spires on the right; caption trim [0.03, 0.04, 0.975, 0.86]. #6 (after Gottheil, 1859–64) is a color view over the Altona station but only 1024 px. #1 (Probst optical print, 1740) and #5 (1770) are views from Hamburg looking toward Altona; in #5 Altona is only a thin strip on the horizon, and #1 shows Hamburg’s harbor, so both skipped. #2–#4 (Strack, 1811) show Baur’s Park in Blankenese, then a separate village. #9 is an aerial of one 1928 housing block. #10–#13 are aerials of Blankenese, part of the modern borough but not the old city.
